newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-RUSSIA 1997 GRAIN OUTPUT AROUND 80 MLN T.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-RUSSIA 1997 GRAIN OUTPUT AROUND 80 MLN T.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
RUSSIAN GRAIN OUTPUT REVISED UPWARDS TO AROUND 80 MLN TONNES

Russian net grain output is likely to reach between 76 and 82 million tonnes, around 15 percent up on last year, as higher yields boost output forecasts for all regions in the European part of the country and in the Urals.

But the updated estimate remains below the 1991-95 average for Russian grain harvests and farmers continue to face constrained domestic demand due to the prolonged decline in the Russian livestock sector.

Russia is therefore likely to be looking to increase its grain exports in 1997/98, particularly of feed wheat. But the country faces strong competition from Ukrainian and East European feed wheat producers.

The harvest in the south area of the European part of Russia (North Caucasus, the Black Earth and Povolzhsk regions), and in the Urals, started about one week later than last year due to wet and cool weather in the region.
But heavy rains helped boost yields in most regions of the European part of Russia and the Urals.
Average yields from the threshed area are about 25-30 percent up on last year, particularly in Povolzhsk, the Urals and Central Chernozem (the Black Earth) regions.
But at the same time abundant rains in July have damaged crop quality, particularly wheat.
In the North Caucasus and Povolzhsk, which account for about 60 percent of total milling wheat production, feed wheat accounts for 50-75 percent of total output so far.
The share of feed wheat is particularly high in Rostov oblast (the North Caucasus) and Saratov and Volgograd oblast (Povolzhsk region).
